institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a german speaking university and country. Also the mountains near Wien.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my study abroad and the BOKU university was very nice! I did though often feel very helpless in all the administrative parts of the exchange, and it did have a very negative influence on my stress-level and the overall experience. I spend a lot of time trying to figure out everything with mobility online and language qualifications and so on. This could have been in my opinion way better structured...

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. BOKU's webpage is okay for giving information. The information i needed from KU was difficult to find, and I never really figured out who my coordinator from KU was...

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a "Buddy" who showed me around, and offered me basic help with stuff. She was on her first year, so she didn't know quite enough about course selection, which was what I needed most help on. The introduction days, were really helpfull!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. WG-gesucht is the perfect app for finding flat-shares in Wien!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Wien is a large city, and public transportation from one end to the other takes quite some time. Find a place as to the campus as possible!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: REALLY BAD!!!! All courses are very small, 3-4 ects in average. And the classes aren't regular so you have to spend a lot of time figuring out how much different courses classes overlap, and whether or not it is okay for the type of course. It was very very stressful and I felt very lost in the process. I know that BOKU is going to change the system soon, to a similar system as the one we have at KU.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can register for course from start Feb and then every course has a different end date for last registration and deregistration. You often get waitlisted for a course, and then have to show up for first class and try to get a spot. You have to write a lot of emails to a lot of professors explaining your situation. It is chaotic to say the least.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a counseling session with a coordinator... It did not help at all, if anything it made it even worse and more confusing.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Well after the first 1,5 month of going to a 100 different classes and professors I settled on 10 courses that I was quite satisfied with.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write me an email, and I will try to help you. Also don't be too scared of the overlapping, the professors really understand the situation, and are aware you can't make it for every class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very different from KU, but really interesting and very good teachers!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I almost only did MA courses. There aren't a lot of electives at landscaping architecture BA, or at least I didn't find them. It is fine to take the MA courses though.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some things were similar, some different. The courses had fewer students which made it easy to have direct communication with the professor. There are tutors for every course almost. Yeah the style was in many ways similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Climbing class was GREAT

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of nice social events at the UNI! I enjoyed seeing three shows at volksoper while is was there. The museums and gardens of Wien is really nice as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to Spronsertag or for a trip to Salzburg or just to donau. The climbing gyms in Wien are amazing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the mountains or the nearby cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time for me, but it is quite similar to DK.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just smile and speak to them. They don't nessicarily take contact themselves but they are very openminded and very friendly and helpfull!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Well the language barriere is always there, but in general it wasn't that bad.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: very down to earth easy going among young people. A lot of art in the city. I did miss the music culture scene from back home in Copenhagen though.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy Ilse-Wallentin Haus it is a great place to do your studies. Use the TÜWI for hanging out, people there are very openminded, and also spend some of your breaks in Türkenschantzpark!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be affraid of taking german courses, the teachers are very helpful and flexible with the language barriere.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know how austrian students structure their studylife and work as future landscape architects.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Joggling 10 different courses and doing 10 exams at one time within a month, where most of them where project based and with inly german litterature... yeah...

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.answer: Yes
